title: One procedure run contract across Lambda, Fargate and local-pod runtimes (L)
description:
Define one run contract that every procedure run follows, whatever the trigger and wherever it runs: load the published version, record the run, execute, write back. This replaces the four paths (CLI cloud-source fetch, assignment-action key dispatch, runner Lambda, Fargate construct from PPY-dca7cd).

Scope:
- The shared contract, with three runtimes: the papyrus-procedure-runner Lambda (default); Fargate for procedures marked long or heavy; local pod (the local-pod runtime is built in PPY-93faf2).
- A per-procedure runtime field (lambda | container | local) on the definition, defaulting to lambda.
- The Fargate runtime reuses the Step Functions + Fargate construct from PPY-dca7cd, driven by the contract.
- Guardrails in the contract: a cost estimate per run; the projection lease for anything touching pages, and never reconcile; failure before projection leaves the site unchanged; idempotency keys and a run record.
- Retire amplify/functions/assignment-action's fixed key dispatch; its kinds run through the contract.
- The knowledge pipeline is expressed as a container-runtime automation (stale-checkout guard and projection-deletion guard preserved). PPY-dca7cd remains blocked on Ryan's approval to run it in AWS.
- The trend-story pipeline (PPY-fb4dfa) uses the contract instead of its own runner.

Acceptance criteria:
- The same procedure runs unchanged on the Lambda and container runtimes and records the same ProcedureRun shape.
- A deliberate failure on each runtime stops before projection and leaves the site unchanged.
- assignment-action no longer dispatches by fixed key.
- CDK assertions for the container runtime; one example automation configured but disabled.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) required.

Depends on PPY-1b2edd.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Findings from the local-run exercise (2026-10-23): there is no readiness check, so add 'papyrus knowledge status' to report a site's knowledge config, accepted-reference counts, state location and pins. Site discovery is awkward: AppSync ids live only in nested stacks or the amplify:app-id tag, so add a site registry. The SDK's SSO refresh fails, so export CLI credentials. Ideas dedupe memory and the run ledger are local only. TI isn't ready for a knowledge run: it has no vocabulary, beats or wiki config and only 11 accepted references.
